ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r6.claim: Arrogant deniers of the Qur'an and Prophet are warned; their worldly affluence fuels their arrogance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r6.anchor: people who are denying the Qur’ān and the Prophet (sws) because of arrogance are warned.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p540/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p540/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p540/r6.claim: The next section attacks love of transient worldly life as the reason disbelievers have hardened hearts and become averse to the Qur’an.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p540/r6.anchor: the reason which led the disbelievers to show indifference to the Qur’ān is attacked: it is their love for this transient life

ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r6.claim: The rain's sky is interpreted as either God's presence or the heart; the water is knowledge and insight, the channels are faculties, and the earth is human nature.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r6.anchor: من سماء حضرته سبحانه أو من سماء القلب ( ماء ) ماء المعارف والعلوم ( فسلكه ينابيع ) مدارك وقوى ( في الأرض ) أرض البشرية

ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r7.claim: The crop represents bodily deeds and spoken words; its yellowing and collapse represent ostentatious acts that first look sound, then wither into regret.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r7.anchor: ثم يخرج به زرعا ) من الأعمال البدنية والأقوال اللسانية ( ثم يهيج فتراه مصفرا ثم يجعله حطاما ) إشارة إلى أفعال المرائين

SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r1.claim: The common reading has ثم يجعله in the indicative, coordinated with the preceding verb.
SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r1.anchor: العامة على رفع الفعل نسقا على ما قبله.

SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r2.speaker: أبو بشر
SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r2.claim: Abu Bishr reads ثم يجعله in the accusative; al-Hudhali in al-Kāmil calls this weak, and al-Samīn agrees because no apparent preceding element licenses it.
SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو بشر " ثم يجعله " منصوبا. قال الشيخ: " قال صاحب الكامل: " وهو ضعيف " انتهى.

SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r3.claim: One parse supplies أن and coordinates the clause with أن الله أنزل earlier in the verse.
SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r3.anchor: أن ينتصب بإضمار " أن " ويكون معطوفا على قوله: { أن الله أنزل من السمآء مآء }

SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r4.claim: A second parse supplies ترى as governor, with implicit أن making the clause its object: then you see it made into debris.
SAMIN-DURR:39:21/r4.anchor: أن يكون منصوبا بتقدير ترى أي: ثم ترى جعله حطاما،

ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r9.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r9.claim: Tafsīr says that everything on earth originates from heaven.
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r9.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن كل ما في الأرض فابتداؤه من السماء

ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r10.claim: ينابيع are places where water springs forth; the singular is ينبوع, measured as yَفْعول from نبع ينبع.
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r10.anchor: ومعنى " ينابيع " الأمكنة التي ينبع منها الماء،

ASAD-NOTES:39:21#n26/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:21#n26/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:21#n26/r1.claim: Nature's repeated transformations and life-death cycle demonstrate God's might, especially His power to resurrect the dead.
ASAD-NOTES:39:21#n26/r1.anchor: the above Qur'anic reference to the endless transformations and the miraculous cycle of life and death in all nature serves to emphasize God's almightiness and, specifically, His power to resurrect the dead

ASAD-NOTES:39:21#n26/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:21#n26/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:21#n26/r2.claim: The natural cycle indirectly recalls the preceding verse's assurance that God never fails to fulfil His promise.
ASAD-NOTES:39:21#n26/r2.anchor: thus alluding, indirectly, to the statement at the end of the preceding verse that "never does God fail to fulfil His promise".

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p578/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p578/r1.speaker: ابن فارس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p578/r1.claim: Ibn Faris defines the root as a sound origin for what takes a person outside the limit of health in any matter.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p578/r1.anchor: قال ابن فارس فى (مرض) : الميم والراء والضاد: أصل صحيح يدل على

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p578/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p578/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p578/r2.claim: In Qur'anic legal verses, marad, marid, al-marid, and marḍa denote bodily illness; illness of the heart or hearts shifts metaphorically from the root sense.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p578/r2.anchor: فحيثما جاء المرض فى آيات الأحكام فهو من علة فى البدن. وكذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r1.claim: The passage either compares worldly life's quick disappearance to the crop's cycle, warning against its beauty, or adduces rain and its effects as evidence for the promised rivers beneath the chambers.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r1.anchor: استئناف وارد إما لتمثيل الحياة الدنيا في سرعة الزوال وقرب الإضمحلال بما ذكر من أحوال الزرع

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r2.claim: The water is rain, and heaven means the direction above.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r2.anchor: والمراد بالماء المطر وبالسماء جهة العلو

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r3.claim: Another view takes heaven as the celestial bodies, since rain descends through causes originating there, such as vapor rising and clouds forming through the sun's attraction and changing positions.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r3.anchor: وقيل : الأجرام العلوية وكون إنزال المطر منها باعتبار أنه بأسباب ناشئة منها

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r4.claim: The claim that rain itself falls directly from the familiar celestial sphere is undermined by heavy rain and clouds below a mountain peak where an observer above sees neither cloud nor rain.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r4.anchor: وأما كون إنزال المطر نفسه من جرم السماء المعروفة نفسها فكثيرا ما يرتفع سحاب ويمطر مطرا غزيرا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r5.claim: Some take the water as all water on earth and the descent as occurring at creation, when God sent water from the Sea of the Throne onto the newly created, waterless earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r5.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالماء كل ماء في الأرض والمراد بالإنزال المذكور الإنزال في مبدأ الخليقة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r6.claim: Sālaka means He inserted it; springs and channels are conduits in the earth like veins in bodies. On the rain view the verse appears to make spring and canal water rainwater, unlike the creation-origin view.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r6.anchor: أي في ينابيع أي عيون ومجاري كائنة في الأرض كالعروق في الأجساد

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r7.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r7.claim: Philosophers say underground vapor is trapped, cools and becomes water mixed with vapor, then ruptures the earth when it accumulates and forms springs.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r7.anchor: وشاع عن الفلاسفة أن ماء العيون وما يجري مجراها من الأبخرة قالوا : إن البخار إذا احتبس في الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r8.speaker: أبو البركات البغدادي
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r8.claim: Abū al-Barakāt al-Baghdādī rejects vapor as the cause of springs: they are meltwater and rainwater, increasing and decreasing with precipitation; underground condensation predicts the opposite seasonal pattern from observed springs and wells.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r8.anchor: ورده أبو البركات البغدادي فقال في المعتبر : السبب في العيون وما يجري مجراها هو يسيل من الثلوج ومياه الأمطار

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r9.speaker: الميبدي
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r9.claim: Al-Mībudhī says the precipitation explanation is certainly valid, but its evidence only shows vapor cannot be the sole cause, not that it contributes at all.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255/r9.anchor: قال الميبدي : الحق أن السبب الذي ذكره صاحب المعتبر معتبر لا محالة إلا أنه غير مانع من اعتبار السبب الذي ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r1.speaker: شرح المواقف
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r1.claim: Sharḥ al-Mawāqif presents two accounts of water: scattered aqueous matter deep underground joining together, or vaporous air turning to water; the latter is possible, but the former is stronger because springs and wells rise with snow and rain.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r1.anchor: اختلفوا في أن المياه متولدة من أجزاء مائية متفرقة في عمق الأرض إذا اجتمعت أو من الهواء البخاري

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī takes the verse's water to mean rain and similar precipitation such as snow; it says God leads this water into springs, not that every part of spring water has that sole origin, allowing some to arise from condensed vapor.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r2.anchor: والأولى عندي أن يحمل الماء في الآية على المطر ونحوه من الثلج والآية تدل على أن ذلك الماء يسلكه الله تعالى في ينابيع

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r3.claim: Reading the water as the creation-era supply lacks a sound report and strongly departs from the apparent verse: the general address “Do you not see?” cannot apply to witnessing creation, forcing an implausibly specific address to the Prophet by revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r3.anchor: وحمل الإنزال على الإنزال في مبدأ الخليقة على ما سمعت مع كونه مما لم أقف على خبر صحيح يقتضيه خلاف الظاهر في الآية جدا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī cites the view that all earth's water descends from heaven to a rock and God distributes it among regions.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r4.anchor: ما حكاه الزمخشري في الآية عن بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says all water on earth is sent down by God from heaven, while underground veins alter it; a similar report is attributed to Saʿīd b. Jubayr and al-Shaʿbī. If authentic and treated as marfūʿ, al-Ālūsī says its literal sense is acceptable because reason does not limit God's power.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال في الآية : ليس في الأرض ماء إلا ما أنزال الله تعالى من السماء ولكن عروق في الأرض تغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r6.claim: Yānābīʿ could be the plural of yānbiʿ meaning a flowing thing, then an accusative circumstantial expression for water flowing in earth; this is awkward, since min al-arḍ would be expected.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r6.anchor: وجوز أن تكون الينابيع جمع ينبوع بمعنى النابع فإنه كما يطلق على المنبع يطلق على ما ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r7.claim: On the usual sense of springs, yānābīʿ is accusative by omission of a preposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r7.anchor: وعلى ما هو المشهور يكون ( ينابيع ) منصوبا بنزع الخافض كما أشرنا إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r8.claim: Treating yānābīʿ as a cognate accusative requires distant ellipses, either deleting a verbal noun and supplying its description or deleting a genitive noun from “flowing of springs.”
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r8.anchor: واحتمال كونه منصوبا على المصدرية في إطلاقيه بأن يكون الأصل فسلكه سلوكا في ينابيع

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r9.claim: The phrase means God brings forth crops by means of water in keeping with wisdom, not because water is intrinsically necessary to the act; the Ashʿarites read it as occurring alongside water with no causal role for it.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r9.anchor: أي بواسطته مراعاة للحكمة لا لتوقف الإخراج عليه في نفس الأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r10.claim: Different colors can mean different crop kinds such as wheat and barley, visible qualities such as green and red, or every perceptible quality including color and taste; the wording covers food and other crops.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r10.anchor: أي أنواعه وأصنافه من بر وشعير وغيرهما أو كيفياته المدركة بالبصر من خضرة وحمرة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r11.claim: Thumma marks delay in time or rank, while the imperfect verb vividly presents the scene.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r11.anchor: وثم للتراخي في الرتبة أو الزمان

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r12.claim: The apparent lexical meaning of yahīju is that the crop dries; some interpreters take it to mean it rises, a figurative use because a fully dried crop is about to break loose from its roots.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r12.anchor: وظاهر كلام أهل اللغة أن هذا معنى حقيقي للهيجان

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r13.claim: A variant reading has muṣfārran for the standard muṣfarran, describing the crop turning yellow after its greenness and freshness.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r13.anchor: من بعد خضرته ونضارته وقريء ( مصفارا )

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r14.claim: Ḥuṭām means broken, crumbling fragments; because this forceful change is among the effects, its production is expressly ascribed to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r14.anchor: فتاتا متكسرا كأن لم يغن بالأمس ولكون هذه الحالة من الآثار القوية علقت بجعل الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r15.speaker: أبو بشر
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r15.claim: Abū Bishr reads the verb after thumma in the accusative; the source's citation from al-Kāmil calls this reading weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p255#2/r15.anchor: وقرأ أبو بشر ( ثم يجعله ) بالنصب قال صاحب الكامل وهو ضعيف

ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī agrees that the accusative reading is weak and points to the cited poetic construction, إني وقتلي سليكا ثم أعقله, as its grammatical parallel.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r1.anchor: إني وقتلي سليكا ثم أعقله ولا يخفى وجه ضعفه هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r2.claim: “In that” points back to all the details just described, and the demonstrative's distance signals their extraordinary significance and evidentiary force.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r2.anchor: إشارة إلى ما ذكر تفصيلا وما فيه من معنى البعد للإيذان ببعد منزلته في الغرابة والدلالة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r3.claim: The scene is a great reminder for people of sound intellect, whose minds are free of defects.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r3.anchor: لأصحاب العقول الخالصة عن شوائب الخلل وتنبيها لهم على حقيقة الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r4.claim: The cycle reminds them that worldly life passes quickly, so they should not be deceived by its beauty or captivated by its temptations.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r4.anchor: يتذكرون بذلك حال الحياة الدنيا وسرعة تقضيها فلا يغترون ببهجتها ولا يفتنون بفتنها

ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r5.claim: Another application is that the One who sends rain and governs it perfectly can bring about the promised rivers beneath the chambers.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r5.anchor: أو يجزمون بأن من قدر على إنزال الماء من السماء والتصرف به على أتم وجه قادر على إجراء الأنهار من تحت تلك الغرف

ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the first reminder: the preceding passage encourages the afterlife, while this image warns against worldly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r6.anchor: وكأن الأول أولى ليكون ما تقدم ترغيبا في الآخرة وهذا تنفيرا عن الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r7.claim: A further view makes the scene a reminder that a wise maker must have brought it about through determination and design, not neglect.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r7.anchor: وقيل المعنى إن في ذلك لتذكيرا وتنبيها على أنه لا بد لذلك من صانع حكيم وأنه كائن على تقدير وتدبير

ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds that creator-proof reading far from the context: because the effects are explicitly ascribed to God, the reminder concerns God's acts or their implications, rather than proving His existence.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p256/r8.anchor: بمعزل عما يقتضيه السياق على أن الأنسب بإرادة ذلك ذكر الآثار غير مسندة إليه عز وجل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p435/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p435/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p435/r9.claim: The Prophet is urged to reflect on recurring evidence that God can restore what has decayed, been torn apart, and dispersed.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p435/r9.anchor: وخص المصطفى صلى الله عليه وسلم بالخطاب حثا على تأمل هذا الدليل تنبيها على عظمته

BIQAI-FULL:v6p435/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p435/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p435/r10.claim: Rain's descent and measured amount display God's power: water remains in the sky only by His compelling it, then He sends it down in a managed order.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p435/r10.anchor: التي لا يستمسك الماء فيها إلا بقدرة باهرة تقهره على ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v6p435/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p435/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p435/r11.claim: God makes the water rise as gushing springs after hiding it in the earth's depths, another recurring sign of His control.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p435/r11.anchor: فقهره على الصعود بعد أن غيبه في أعماقها بالفيض والصوب بعد أن كان قسره على الانضباط في العلو

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says all water in the earth came down from the sky, while veins in the earth alter it; he explains the verse as God directing it into springs and says anyone who wants salt water to become fresh should ascend.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى : الم تر ان الله انزل من السماء ماء فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض قال : ليس في الأرض ماء الا نزل من السماء

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249#2/r2.speaker: أسماء
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249#2/r2.claim: Asma describes the Companions responding to Quran as God describes: their eyes wept and their skins shivered; she sought refuge from Satan when told that some listeners fainted.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249#2/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عروة بن الزبير قال : قلت لجدتي اسماء رضي الله عنهما كيف كان يصنع اصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اذا قراوا القران

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249#2/r3.speaker: علي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249#2/r3.claim: When accused of judging as a disbeliever and hypocrite, Ali replied that he had judged no created person and had judged only by the Quran.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249#2/r3.anchor: عن الفرج بن زيد الكلاعي رضي الله عنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r8.claim: God directs the Prophet to consider a sign among created things; the address also includes every human being.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r8.anchor: ثم وقف نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم على معتبر من مخلوقاته، والخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وكل بشر داخل معه في معناه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r9.speaker: الطبري وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and others identify the water as rainwater, arguing that springs appear when rain comes and dry when it is absent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r9.anchor: وقال الطبري وغيره: أشار إلى ماء المطر، وقالوا: العيون منه، ودليل ذلك أنها تنماع عند وجوده وتيبس عند فقده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r10.speaker: الحسن بن مسلم بن يناق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim ibn Yannāq says the reference is to springs, whose water comes down from the sky rather than deriving from rain itself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن بن مسلم بن يناق، والإشارة إلى العيون وليست العيون من المطر، ولكن ماؤها نازل من السماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r11.claim: The rainwater and spring-water explanations are close to one another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r11.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: والقولان متقاربان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r12.speaker: الشعبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r12.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says every fresh water on earth descended from the sky.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r12.anchor: قال الشعبي: وكل ماء عذب في الأرض فمن السماء نزل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r13.claim: Salakahu means that God made the water flow or inserted it into the earth; the cited line uses the verb for driving something through.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r13.anchor: و: «سلكه» معناه: أجراه وأدخله، ومنه قول الشاعر [البسيط] حتى سلكن الشوى منهن في مسك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r14.claim: Yanābīʿ is an intensive form derived from nabʿ, the act of welling up; ʿayn is one kind of spring.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r14.anchor: وواحد الينابيع وهو العين بني لها بناء مبالغة من النبع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r15.claim: The word zarʿ here covers everything that is cultivated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r15.anchor: والزرع هنا واقع على كل ما يزرع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r16.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r16.claim: One group understands the differing colors as qualities such as redness and yellowness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r16.anchor: وقالت فرقة: ألوانه أعراضه من الحمرة والصفرة وغير ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r17.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r17.claim: Another group understands the differing colors as kinds of crops, such as wheat, rice, and maize.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r17.anchor: وقالت فرقة: ألوانه أنواعه من القمح والأرز والذرة وغير ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r18.claim: Yahīj means that the vegetation dries; the verb is used of plants when they dry out.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r18.anchor: و: يهيج ييبس، هاج النبات والزرع إذا يبس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r19.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r19.claim: A saying attributed to ʿAlī in a report cited in Ibn Qutayba's Gharīb says that a community's crop does not wither from piety, nor does a root-stock dry up upon piety.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r19.anchor: ذمتي رهينة وأنا به زعيم. أي لا يهيج عن التقوى زرع قوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r20.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r20.claim: Ḥuṭām is what has become dry and crumbled.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r21.claim: The crop's cycle is a reminder of resurrection from the graves and the revival of the dead.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p526/r21.anchor: ومعنى قوله: لذكرى أي للبعث من القبور وإحياء الموتى على ما يوجبه هذا المثال المذكور

BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r1.claim: The fragment notes a manuscript vocalization with damma and specifies fatḥa on the imperfect prefix and lām in la tablā; the antecedent falls outside this excerpt.
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r1.anchor: وفي بعض النسخ بضمها ؛ أي : لا يرى شدة قوله : لا تبلى بفتح حرف المضارعة واللام.

BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r2.claim: The address may be directed to Muhammad or to any observer.
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r2.anchor: {ألم تر} . (آيا نمى بينى يا محمد) ، أو يا أيها الناظر.

BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r3.claim: The water sent down from heaven is rain, which Bursevi locates beneath the Throne before its descent.
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r3.anchor: أن الله أنزل من السمآء} من تحت العرش {مآء} هو المطر.

BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra relates from the Prophet that sweet waters and pollinating winds come from beneath Jerusalem's rock; Bursevi says earthly waters descend through clouds to that rock, then God distributes them among lands.
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r4.anchor: روي عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي عليه السلام أنه قال : "المياه العذبة والرياح اللواقح من تحت صخرة بيت المقدس"

BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r5.claim: Salaka means to enter or lead something into a place, while aslaka means to insert it; God channels and arranges the water within earth.
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r5.anchor: وسلك غيره فيه ، وأسلكه : أدخله فيه

BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r6.claim: Springs are eyes and channels through earth, like veins in bodies.
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r6.anchor: ينابيع فى الأرض} ؛ أي : عيونا ومجاري كالعروق في الأجساد فقوله : {ينابيع}

BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r7.claim: Yanabia is accusative after omission of a preposition, as in the explicit preposition in the command to put one's hand into the pocket.
BURSEVI:v8p69#3/r7.anchor: نصب بنزع الخافض. وقد ذكر الخافض في قوله : {اسلك يدك فى جيبك}

BURSEVI:v8p70/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p70/r1.claim: In the earth specifies where springs are, like telling someone to put water into the garden's irrigation channel.
BURSEVI:v8p70/r1.anchor: وقوله : {فى الأرض} بيان لمكان الينابيع كقولك لصاحبك : أدخل الماء في جدول المبطخة في البستان

BURSEVI:v8p70/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p70/r2.claim: Spring water is rain stored in earth and released little by little.
BURSEVI:v8p70/r2.anchor: وفيه أن ماء العين هو المطر يحبسه في الأرض ، ثم يخرجه شيئا فشيئا

BURSEVI:v8p70/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p70/r3.claim: Yanabi is plural of yanbu, a spring from which water emerges; the plural names places where water wells up.
BURSEVI:v8p70/r3.anchor: فالينابيع جمع ينبوع ، وهو يفعول من نبع الماء ينبع مثلثة ونبوعا خرج من العين.

BURSEVI:v8p70/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p70/r4.claim: Zar is originally a verbal noun meaning growth or planting, but here refers to the cultivated crop.
BURSEVI:v8p70/r4.anchor: هو في الأصل مصدر بمعنى الإنبات عبر به عن المزروع

BURSEVI:v8p70/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p70/r5.claim: Varied colors refer to crop species such as wheat and barley and to qualities such as color and taste.
BURSEVI:v8p70/r5.anchor: أصنافه إضافة من بر وشعير وغيرهما

BURSEVI:v8p70/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p70/r6.claim: Thumma can mark delay in rank or time, while the imperfect verb makes the scene vivid to the listener.
BURSEVI:v8p70/r6.anchor: وكلمة ثم للتراخي في الرتبة أو الزمان ، وصيغة المضارع لاستحضار الصورة.

BURSEVI:v8p70/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70/r7.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p70/r7.claim: Al-Raghib says color includes white, black, and mixtures; colors can also mean species, as in varieties of speech or food.
BURSEVI:v8p70/r7.anchor: قال في "المفردات" : اللون معروف وينطوي على الأبيض والأسود وما يركب منهما.

BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r1.claim: The crop dries when it is time to rise from its growing place; hajja can mean to stir or become dry, as said of plants.
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r1.anchor: أي : يتم جفافه حين حان له أن يثور عن منبته يقال : هاج يهيج هيجا وهيجانا

BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r2.claim: The crop turns yellow after drying from its former greenness and freshness.

BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r3.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r3.claim: Al-Raghib places yellow between black and white, nearer to white, and says it can therefore sometimes signify black.
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r3.anchor: قال الراغب : الصفرة لون من الألوان التي بين السواد والبياض ، وهي إلى البياض أقرب

BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r4.claim: God is the one who makes the crop into debris.
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r4.anchor: أي : الله تعالى {حطاما} ، فتاتا متكسرا كأن لم يغن بالأمس

BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r5.claim: Hutam means shattered fragments; a dry branch is said to break into pieces.
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r5.anchor: تحطم العود إذا تفتت من اليبس

BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r6.claim: Because this forceful transformation is an effect of God's action, the verse attributes it to His making, as it attributes growth to Him.
BURSEVI:v8p70#2/r6.anchor: ولكون هذه الحالة من الآثار القوية علقت بجعل الله تعالى كالإخراج.

BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r1.claim: The detailed cycle is a great reminder for people whose intellect is clear of defects, awakening them to reality.
BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r1.anchor: أصحاب العقول الخالصة من شوائب الخلل وتنبيها لهم على حقيقة الحال

BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r2.claim: Worldly life passes quickly, like a crop that becomes debris each year; people should not be deceived by its beauty or tempted by its trials.
BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r2.anchor: يتذكرون بذلك أن حال الحياة الدنيا في سرعة التقضي والانصرام كما يشاهدونه من حال الحطام كل عام فلا يغترون ببهجتها

BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r3.claim: A Persian poem likens worldly life to a fresh spring meadow whose green leaves disappear when autumn's hard wind blows.
BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r3.anchor: بود حال دنيا جو آن سبزه زار كه بس تازه بينى بفصل بهار جو بروى وزد تند باد خزان

BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r4.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r4.claim: Kashf al-Asrar maps the crop's course onto human life from childhood through old age and death; as grain has value when its seed is harvested, a person has value when emptied of self.
BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r4.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : الإشارة في هذه الآية إلى أن الإنسان يكون طفلا ، ثم شابا ثم كهلا ثم شيخا

BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r5.claim: Al-Tawilat al-Najmiyya reads the opening as spiritual effusion descending from the sky of the heart.
BURSEVI:v8p70#3/r5.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير بقوله : {ألم تر} إلخ ، إلى إنزال ماء الفيض الروحاني من سماء القلب.

BURSEVI:v8p70#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70#4/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p70#4/r1.claim: The spiritual water flows as channels of wisdom through human nature and produces bodily acts as a crop whose colors are prayer, almsgiving, fasting, pilgrimage, and jihad.
BURSEVI:v8p70#4/r1.anchor: {فسلكه ينابيع} الحكمة {فى الأرض} البشرية. {ثم يخرج به زرعا} ، من الأعمال البدنية.

BURSEVI:v8p70#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70#4/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p70#4/r2.claim: Show-offs' deeds first look green and compliant with law, then dry through vanity and ostentation; they yellow without light and are shattered by divine severity, leaving regret.
BURSEVI:v8p70#4/r2.anchor: يشير إلى أعمال المرائي تراها مخضرة على وفق الشرع ، ثم تجف من آفة العجب والرياء.

BURSEVI:v8p70#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p70#4/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p70#4/r3.claim: A wayfarer first shows effort through reason and learning; ascent to gnosis dissolves that state, then unity's light consumes sciences and gnoses like sunlight extinguishing stars, bringing a new state of abiding after annihilation.
BURSEVI:v8p70#4/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى أن السالك إذا جرى على مقتضى عقله وعلمه يظهر منه آثار الاجتهاد ، ثم إذا ترقى إلى مقام المعرفة تضمحل منه حالته الأولى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r1.claim: The water is rain; another view says all water on earth descends from the sky to a rock, from which God distributes it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r1.anchor: يعنى المطر وقيل كل ماء فى الأرض فهو من السماء ينزل منها إلى الصخرة ثم يقسمه الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r2.claim: He made the water enter the earth; yanābīʿ are springs, channels, and conduits like veins in bodies.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r2.anchor: ﴿ فسلكه ﴾ فأدخله ﴿ ينابيع في الأرض ﴾ عيونا ومسالك ومجارى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r3.claim: Yanābīʿ is accusative either as a circumstantial accusative or as an adverbial; fī al-arḍ qualifies yanābīʿ.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r3.anchor: وينابيع نصب على الحال أو على الظرف وفى الأرض صفة لينابيع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r4.claim: The plants are brought forth by the water.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r4.anchor: ﴿ ثم يخرج به ﴾ بالماء ﴿ زرعا مختلفا ألوانه ﴾ هيئاته

NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r5.claim: Different colors may mean appearances such as green, red, yellow, and white, or different crops such as wheat, barley, and sesame.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r5.anchor: هيئاته من خضرة وحمرة وصفرة وبياض أو أصنافه من بر وشعير وسمسم وغير ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r6.claim: The crop dries and yellows after its freshness and beauty.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r6.anchor: ﴿ ثم يهيج ﴾ يجف ﴿ فتراه مصفرا ﴾ بعد نضارته وحسنه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r7.claim: Ḥuṭām is plant matter or other material that has crumbled and broken apart.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r7.anchor: فتاتا متكسرا فالحطام ما تفتت وتكسر من النبت وغيره

NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r8.claim: Rain and growth remind rational people that a wise Maker exists and that creation proceeds by measure and design, not neglect or idleness.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51#4/r8.anchor: لتذكيرا وتنبيها على أنه لا بد من صانع حكيم وان ذلك كائن عن تقدير وتدبير لا عن إهمال وتعطيل

QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r1.claim: The water cycle shows that God can resurrect creation, keep His promise, and distinguish believer from unbeliever, just as He can send rain.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r1.anchor: أي إنه لا يخلف الميعاد في إحياء الخلق، والتمييز بين المؤمن والكافر، وهو قادر على ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r2.claim: The water from heaven means rain from the clouds.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r3.claim: God inserted the water into the earth and settled it there, as stated in 23:18.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r3.anchor: أي فأدخله في الأرض وأسكنه فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r4.claim: Yanābīʿ is the plural of yanbūʿ, an outlet or spring, and the text gives several vowel forms for the verb yanaʿ.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r4.anchor: جمع ينبوع وهو يفعول من نبع ينبع وينبع وينبع

QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r5.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r5.claim: Al-Nahhas transmits Ibn Kaysan’s explanation that poetic yanbāʿ elongates the fatḥa in yanbaʿ into an alif.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r5.anchor: النحاس: وحكى لنا ابن كيسان في قول الشاعر: ينباع من ذفرى غضوب جسرة

QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r6.claim: The generic word zarʿ means many kinds of crops in varied colors, including red, yellow, blue, green, and luminous or white.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r6.anchor: هو للجنس أي زروعا شتى لها ألوان مختلفة

QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r7.speaker: الشعبي والضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbi and al-Dahhak say all water on earth came from the sky, first reaching a rock and then dividing into springs and wells.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r7.anchor: قال الشعبي والضحاك: كل ماء في الأرض فمن السماء نزل، إنما ينزل من السماء إلى الصخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r8.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r8.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says hayaja describes plants receding and fading; hājat al-arḍ means its vegetation has passed or withered.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r8.anchor: قال الأصمعي: يقال هاجت الأرض تهيج إذا أدبر نبتها وولى

QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r9.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r9.claim: Al-Jawhari says hayaja is when a plant dries; a barren field has dry or yellowed vegetation, wind dries plants, and the verb also describes anger rising or calming.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r9.anchor: وقال الجوهري: هاج النبت هياجا أي يبس. وأرض هائجة يبس بقلها أو اصفر

QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r10.claim: Ḥuṭām means broken fragments, from dry wood breaking into pieces.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r10.anchor: أي فتاتا مكسرا من تحطم العود إذا تفتت من اليبس

QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r11.claim: The one who can bring the plant through these stages can also bring the dead back to life.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r11.anchor: والمعنى أن من قدر على هذا قدر على الإعادة

QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r12.claim: One interpretation makes rain a parable for the Qur’an entering believers’ hearts: it grows varied religion, strengthening believers while a diseased heart withers like a plant.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r12.anchor: وقيل: هو مثل ضربه الله للقرآن ولصدور من في الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r13.claim: Another interpretation makes the plant a parable for worldly life: as green growth turns yellow, the world fades after its beauty.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r13.anchor: وقيل: هو مثل ضربه الله للدنيا أي كما يتغير النبت الأخضر فيصفر

QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r14.claim: The signs in the water and plant cycle offer a reminder to people of understanding.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:21/r14.anchor: إن في ذلك لذكرى لأولي الألباب

QASHANI:39:17-21/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:17-21/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:17-21/r10.claim: The sky is the spirit and its rain is knowledge, which sends springs of wisdom into souls according to their capacities.
QASHANI:39:17-21/r10.anchor: الحكم في أراضي النفوس بحسب استعدادتها

QASHANI:39:17-21/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:17-21/r11.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:17-21/r11.claim: The crop represents deeds and morals, whose kinds vary with the different powers and bodily members.

QASHANI:39:17-21/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:17-21/r12.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:17-21/r12.claim: The crop's withering signifies separation from its root through the lights of manifestations and its fading as the powers, souls, and hearts that upheld it are annihilated.

QASHANI:39:17-21/r13.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:17-21/r13.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:17-21/r13.claim: The crop becomes fragments when divine attributes appear and become established through spiritual realization.
QASHANI:39:17-21/r13.anchor: بذهابه وانكساره وانقشاعه عند ظهور صفاته تعالى واستقرارها بالتمكين

QASHANI:39:21/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:21/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:21/r1.claim: The people of inner cores are spiritual realities stripped of the shell of egohood.

RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r1.claim: The water is rain; an alternative view says everything on earth comes from the sky. God sends the water to places, then distributes it through springs, channels, and underground courses like bodily veins.
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r1.anchor: وهو المطر وقيل كل ما كان في الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r2.claim: The crop's differing colors may mean different hues such as green, red, yellow, and white, or different kinds such as wheat, barley, and sesame.
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r2.anchor: يخرج به زرعا مختلفا ألوانه من خضرة

RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r3.claim: After fully drying, the crop can detach from its roots before its parts break apart; it is as if the parts have stirred in readiness to disperse.
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r3.anchor: إذا تم جفافه جاز له أن ينفصل عن منابته

RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r4.claim: Hutam is the dry plant matter that crumbles and breaks apart.
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r4.anchor: والحطام ما يجف ويتفتت ويكسر من النبت

RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r5.claim: Watching plants age reminds people that animals and humans, however long-lived, will grow old, become yellow and broken, and die; this reflection makes worldly pleasures less alluring.
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r5.anchor: علم أن أحوال الحيوان والإنسان كذلك وأنه وإن طال عمره فلا بد له من الانتهاء إلى أن يصير مصفر اللون منحطم الأعضاء والأجزاء

RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r6.claim: The preceding descriptions of the afterlife promote desire for it, while this world's description promotes aversion; direct encouragement toward the afterlife comes first because it is the primary aim.
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r6.anchor: في الآيات المتقدمة ذكر ما يقوى الرغبة في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r7.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r7.claim: Al-Wahidi derives yanabi from yanbu, on the pattern yaf'ul, from the root n-b-ʿ; al-Kisa'i and al-Farra report three forms for the verb meaning water bubbled forth.

RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r8.claim: Yanabi is accusative with the preposition omitted; the underlying phrase is to direct the water into springs.
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r8.anchor: نصب بحذف الخافض لأن التقدير فسلكه في ينابيع

RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r9.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v26p230/r9.claim: In the lexical discussion, al-Wahidi glosses yahiij as becoming green.

STUDYQURAN:39:21/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:21/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:21/r1.claim: The account of God sending water from the sky is connected to 6:99.
STUDYQURAN:39:21/r1.anchor: God’s sending down water from the sky

STUDYQURAN:39:21/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:21/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:21/r2.claim: The stages of plant life serve as a metaphor for the stages of human life, as in 18:45 and 57:20.
STUDYQURAN:39:21/r2.anchor: the various stages of plant life are posed as a metaphor for the stages of human life

STUDYQURAN:39:21/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:21/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:21/r3.claim: The paired parables show God’s power over all things and that all things perish except God’s Face.
STUDYQURAN:39:21/r3.anchor: Both verses indicate God’s Power over all things and that all things perish, save His Face (28:88)

TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r1.claim: The rain sent from the sky is made to flow as springs in the earth.
TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r1.anchor: من السماء ماء} [الحج: 63] وهو المطر {فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض} [الزمر: 21] يقول: فأجراه عيونا في الأرض

TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r2.claim: Yanābīʿ are springs; the singular yanbūʿ is what gushes up from the earth.
TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r2.anchor: واحدها ينبوع، وهو ما جاش من الأرض

TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r3.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says every dew and all water on earth came down from the sky.
TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي، في قوله: {فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض} [الزمر: 21] قال: «كل ندى وماء في الأرض من السماء نزل»

TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r4.speaker: الحسن بن مسلم بن بيان
TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim ibn Bayān explains the crop's differing colors as different kinds, including wheat, barley, sesame, and rice.
TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r4.anchor: عن الحسن بن مسلم بن بيان، قال: " ثم أنبت بذلك الماء الذي أنزله من السماء فجعله في الأرض عيونا زرعا {مختلفا ألوانه}

TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r5.claim: The crop dries after being green; Arabic also describes land as having withered when its greenery dries up.
TAB-FULL:v20p187#2/r5.anchor: ثم ييبس ذلك الزرع من بعد خضرته، يقال للأرض إذا يبس ما فيها من الخضر وذوي: هاجت الأرض، وهاج الزرع

TAB-FULL:v20p189/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p189/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p189/r1.claim: The crop's cycle reminds rational people that its maker can create whatever He wills, restore bodies and accidents, and resurrect the dead in their former state, just as He revives barren land.
TAB-FULL:v20p189/r1.anchor: بعد مماته وإعادته من بعد فنائه، كهيئته قبل فنائه، كالذي فعل بالأرض التي أنزل عليها

SULAMI:v2p195#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p195#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p195#2/r1.claim: Some say intellect has one hundred parts: ninety-nine belong to the Prophet and one is shared equally by believers; they differ across twenty portions in the realities of faith.
SULAMI:v2p195#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : اللب والعقل مائة جزء تسعة وتسعون جزءا في النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وجزء في سائر المؤمنين

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383/r1.claim: Salakahu means God put the water into the earth and made it springs that gush forth.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383/r1.anchor: فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض} أي أدخله [فيها] فجعله ينابيع: عيونا تنبع.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383/r3.claim: Ḥuṭām means broken fragments, like chaff or crumbled debris.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383/r3.anchor: ثم يجعله حطاما} مثل الرفات والفتات.

BURHAN:v2p176/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p176/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p176/r1.claim: Sound exegesis must match its object, avoid omissions, unwarranted additions, and deviation, and attend to literal and figurative senses, composition, lexical relations, and contextual allusions; this yields further benefits.
BURHAN:v2p176/r1.anchor: ويجب ان يتحرى في التفسير مطابقة المفسر وأن يتحرز في ذلك من نقص المفسر عما يحتاج اليه من ايضاح المعنى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r1.claim: In the question to Abraham, أأنت فعلت هذا presumes that the idol-breaking occurred and asks whether he was its agent; the answer likewise disputes attribution rather than occurrence.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r1.anchor: قولهم : ( ﴿ أأنت فعلت هذا ﴾ ) . وقال هو عليه السلام في الجواب : ( ﴿ بل فعله كبيرهم هذا ﴾ )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r2.claim: The hamza in أفعلت asks about the act as something the addressee may or may not have done, while أأنت فعلت sets the act as evident and distinguishes its agent from others.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r2.anchor: فهو يقرره بالفعل من غير أن يردده بينه وبين غيره

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r3.claim: Another use of the hamza denies that an act happened at all, as in challenges to the polytheists' claims about sons and daughters for God.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r3.anchor: ولها مذهب آخر وهو أن يكون لإنكار أن يكون الفعل قد كان من أصله

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r4.claim: Fronting the subject directs denial at the alleged agent, as in asking whether someone said a poem; sometimes that form is used while the intended denial is that the act occurred at all, as with God's alleged permission.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p101/r4.anchor: ومثاله قولك للرجل قد انتحل شعرا : أأنت قلت هذا الشعر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p300/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p300/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p300/r1.claim: To arrange an utterance mentally is to assign ضرب as a predicate of Zayd, Amr as its object, Friday as its time, and discipline as its purpose; without these grammatical choices there is no arrangement.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p300/r1.anchor: العاقل يرتب في نفسه ما يريد أن يتكلم به

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p300/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p300/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p300/r2.claim: Words connect through the relations between their meanings, not merely as sounds; the joke of someone reading half a book depends on the lack of meaningful connection, as Abu Tammam's line indicates.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p300/r2.anchor: لن يتصور أن يكون للفظة تعلق بلفظة أخرى من غير أن تعتبر حال معنى هذه مع معنى تلك

TABATABAI:39:21-22/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r1.claim: The passage returns to the argument for God's lordship, contrasts the guidance and outcomes of the guided and misguided, and presents the Qur'an as guidance.
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r1.anchor: بيان عود إلى بدء من الاحتجاج على ربوبيته تعالى والقول في اهتداء المهتدين وضلال الضالين

TABATABAI:39:21-22/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r2.claim: ينابيع is the plural of ينبوع, a spring or place from which water wells up; نبع means that water flows from a place.
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r2.anchor: قال في المجمع الينابيع جمع ينبوع وهو الذي ينبع منه الماء يقال نبع الماء من موضع كذا إذا فار منه

TABATABAI:39:21-22/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r3.claim: الزرع is vegetation that grows without a trunk.
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r3.anchor: والزرع ما ينبت على غير ساق

TABATABAI:39:21-22/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r4.claim: الشجر is vegetation with a trunk and branches; النبات is the broad term encompassing both.
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r4.anchor: والشجر ما له ساق وأغصان النبات يعم الجميع

TABATABAI:39:21-22/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r5.claim: When a plant هاج, it has dried and reached the limit of dryness.
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r5.anchor: وهاج النبت يهيج هيجا إذا جف وبلغ نهايته في اليبوسة

TABATABAI:39:21-22/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r6.claim: الحطام means the broken bits of straw and herbage.

TABATABAI:39:21-22/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r7.claim: God sends the water into underground springs and channels, like bodily veins carrying their contents from one place to another.
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r7.anchor: أي فأدخله في عيون ومجاري في الأرض هي كالعروق في الأبدان تنقل ما تحمله من جانب إلى جانب

TABATABAI:39:21-22/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r8.claim: The water and plant cycle is evidence that God alone exercises lordship.
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r8.anchor: تحتج على توحده تعالى في الربوبية

TABRISI:39:22/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22/r1.claim: Yanabiʿ are places where water springs forth; nabaʿ describes water gushing from a place.
TABRISI:39:22/r1.anchor: الينابيع جمع ينبوع وهو الموضع الذي ينبع منه الماء. يقال: نبع الماء

TABRISI:39:22/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22/r2.claim: Zarʿ is vegetation without a trunk, shajar has a trunk and branches, and nabat covers both generally.
TABRISI:39:22/r2.anchor: والزرع ما ينبت على غير ساق والشجر ما له ساق وأغصان والنبات يعم الجميع

TABRISI:39:22/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22/r3.claim: A plant heaves when it dries and reaches the end of its dryness; hutam is broken straw or grass, from breaking dry things.
TABRISI:39:22/r3.anchor: وهاج النبت يهيج هيجا إذا جف وبلغ نهايته في اليبوسة والحطام فتات التبن والحشيش

TABRISI:39:22/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22/r4.speaker: النضر
TABRISI:39:22/r4.claim: Al-Nadr says al-Hatim in Mecca names a piece of the Kaaba's stone by the spout, left crushed after the House was raised.
TABRISI:39:22/r4.anchor: قال النضر: لأن البيت رفع وترك ذلك محطوما وهو حجر الكعبة مما يلي الميزاب

TABRISI:39:22/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22/r8.claim: God sends rain into the earth as springs, then brings forth crops of varied kinds and colors, which dry, yellow, and crumble.
TABRISI:39:22/r8.anchor: { فسلكه } أي فأدخل ذلك الماء { ينابيع في الأرض }

TABRISI:39:22/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22/r9.claim: Diverse plants produced from one water and carried through successive states remind sound minds of the Creator and establish the truth of first creation, resurrection, and return.
TABRISI:39:22/r9.anchor: لتذكيرا لذوي العقول السليمة إذا تفكروا في ذلك عرفوا الصانع المحدث وعلموا صحة الابتداء والبعث

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r1.claim: God channels rainwater into springs in the earth; all water in the earth has descended from heaven.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r1.anchor: وهي المواضع التي ينبع منها الماء، وكل ماء في الأرض فمن السماء نزل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r2.claim: Water brings forth crops of different colors; they dry, turn yellow, and crumble into fragments, signs for the reflective of God's oneness and power.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r2.anchor: يذكرون ما لهم من الدلالة في هذا على توحيد الله تعالى وقدرته

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r4.claim: Outwardly, rain makes vegetation green before it dries and becomes stubble; inwardly, this is the human life course from childhood through age and decrepitude to death.
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r4.anchor: أخبر أنه ينزل من السماء المطر فيخرج به الزرع فيخضر ، ثم يأخذ في الجفاف ، ثم يصير هشيما

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r5.claim: The grain is the crop’s purpose and is not gathered until the plant begins to dry; likewise, a person has no worth until they attain arrival.
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r5.anchor: ويقال إن الزرع ما لم يأخذ في الجفاف لا يؤخذ منه الحب ، فالحب هو المقصود منه

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r6.claim: A believer’s intellect first advances knowledge until insight reaches fullness; then the dawning authority of divine knowledge submerges those lights, and the lights of tawhid consume them all.
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r6.anchor: كذلك الإنسان ما لم يحصل من نفسه وصول لا يكون له قدر ولا قيمة

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r7.claim: When the lights of tawhid appear, they absorb the prior lights of insight, as sunrise enfolds the light of the stars.
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r7.anchor: فإذا بدت أنوار التوحيد استهلكت تلك الجملة ، قالوا : فلما استبان الصبح أدرج ضوءه

BURHAN:v2p118/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p118/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p118/r3.claim: When al-lubb means intellect, Qur'anic usage gives the plural al-albāb.
BURHAN:v2p118/r3.anchor: وكذلك لفظ اللب مرادا به العقل كقوله تعالى ﴿ وذكرى لأولي الألباب ﴾ ﴿ لذكرى لأولي الألباب ﴾

BURHAN:v2p145/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p145/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p145/r1.claim: God revealed the Qur'an to be understood, addressing people of intellect, knowledge, understanding, and reflection so they ponder and remember.
BURHAN:v2p145/r1.anchor: وبالجملة فالقرآن كله لم ينزله تعالى إلا ليفهمه ويعلم ويفهم ولذلك خاطب به أولي الألباب

MAJAZ:v2p189/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p189/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p189/r1.claim: The singular of yanābīʿ is yanbūʿ, a spring that gushes from the earth.
MAJAZ:v2p189/r1.anchor: «فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض» (21) واحدها ينبوع وهو ما جاش من الأرض..

MAJAZ:v2p189/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p189/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p189/r2.claim: When vegetation has dried up, it is said to have hāja; the earth hāja when its greenery dries.
MAJAZ:v2p189/r2.anchor: إذا ذوى الرطب كله فقد هاج ويقال: هاجت الأرض وهو إذا ذوى ما فيها من الخضر..

MAJAZ:v2p189/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p189/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p189/r3.claim: After turning yellow, it becomes broken, dried plant matter; ḥuṭām, rufāt, and darīn are equivalent words.
MAJAZ:v2p189/r3.anchor: بعد صفرته أي رفاتا والحطام والرفات والدرين واحد فى كلام العرب وهو ما يبس فتحات من النبات..

NAHHAS:v4p8/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p8/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p8/r1.claim: ينبوع is singular, ينبع is also used, and ينابيع is its plural.
NAHHAS:v4p8/r1.anchor: واحدها ينبوع ويقال ينبع وجمعه ينابيع

NAHHAS:v4p8/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p8/r2.speaker: ابن كيسان
NAHHAS:v4p8/r2.claim: Ibn Kaysan explains the unnamed poet's ينباع as ينبع, lengthening the fatḥa into an alif.
NAHHAS:v4p8/r2.anchor: وحكى لنا ابن كيسان في قول الشاعر ( ينباع من ذفرى غضوب جسرة ) إن معناه ينبع

NAHHAS:v4p8/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p8/r3.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v4p8/r3.claim: Al-Asma'i says the land's plants recede when it هاج; another grammarian agrees.
NAHHAS:v4p8/r3.anchor: قال محمد بن يزيد الأصمعي يقال هاجت الأرض تهيج إذا أدبر نبتها

NAHHAS:v4p8/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p8/r4.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v4p8/r4.claim: حطاما is like dry wood broken into fragments.
NAHHAS:v4p8/r4.anchor: قال من تحطيم العود إذا تفتت من اليبس

NAHHAS:v4p8/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p8/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p8/r5.claim: ذو is the singular of أولو, a collective; some linguists add wāw in writing to distinguish it from إلى.
NAHHAS:v4p8/r5.anchor: واحدها ذو وهو اسم للجمع وزيد في كتابه واو عند بعض أهل اللغة

ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r3.claim: The plant's colors include green, yellow, red, white, and other colors.
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r3.anchor: ألوانه خضرة وصفرة وحمرة وبياض وغير ذلك

ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r4.speaker: الأصمعي
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r4.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says a plant is described as hāja when it has become fully dry.
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r4.anchor: قال الأصمعي يقال للنبت إذا تم جفافه: قد هاج يهيج هيجا

ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r5.claim: Ḥuṭām is plant matter or other material that has crumbled and broken; ruftāt and darīn are comparable terms.
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r5.anchor: الحطام ما تفتت وتكسر من النبت وغيره، ومثل الحطام الرفات والدرين

ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r6.claim: The scene prompts people of understanding to reflect and recognize its evidence for God's oneness.
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r6.anchor: أي تفكر لذوي العقول، فيذكرون ما لهم في هذا من الدلالة على توحيد الله

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p542/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p542/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p542/r1.claim: The Prophet’s warning about the rejecters’ fate seems far-fetched to them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p542/r1.anchor: This verse reminds the rejecters of the Qur’ān that the fate the Prophet (sws) is warning them of at that time seems far-fetched to them;

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r1.claim: The Quraysh’s success intoxicates them, so they cannot imagine their dominance ending even as they witness the world’s mortality.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r1.anchor: intoxicated with their success that they cannot think from where their dominance would see its doom even though they are continuously witnessing the fact that everything of this world is temporary and mortal.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r3.claim: The expression “hāja al-nabāt” means that the vegetation started to dry out.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r3.anchor: the vegetation started to dry out

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r4.claim: The observation of this cycle is a great lesson for people of understanding.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r4.anchor: there is a great lesson for men of understanding in this observation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r5.claim: Because life’s pleasures are temporary, an intelligent person should turn toward the self-sufficient Creator who brought them into existence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r5.anchor: a person of intellect should direct his attention to the Being Who brought all these things into existence and is not dependent on any thing for His existence.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r6.claim: People owe gratitude to their Lord for providing their sustenance and should not direct that gratitude to others.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r6.anchor: it is the natural obligation of people to thank their Lord Who made this arrangement in this world for their sustenance and nourishment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r7.claim: The Creator will hold each person accountable and reward or punish them according to justice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r7.anchor: there must come a day in which He will hold each person accountable for his good and evil deeds

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r8.claim: The author signals that one aspect of the example will be explained in the next verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r8.anchor: one particular aspect shall be explained in the next verse.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r5.claim: هاج الزرع means the crop sprang up from its roots, or, in another gloss, dried out.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r5.anchor: هاج الزرع: ثار من منابته، وقيل: يبس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r6.claim: الحطام is plant matter crumbled after drying.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r5.claim: ألم تر addresses and prompts the listener to consider divine acts that show the world's passing and dissolution.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r5.anchor: ألم تر: خطاب وتوقيف للسامع على ما يعتبر به من أفعال الله الدالة على فناء الدنيا واضمحلالها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r6.claim: God directs rainwater into channels and springs; apparently the springs come from rain stored in the earth and released gradually.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن ماء العيون هو من ماء المطر، تحبسه الأرض ويخرج شيئا فشيئا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r7.claim: The growth of crops through rain recalls God's favor that sustains people's livelihood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r7.anchor: ثم يخرج به زرعا، ذكر منته تعالى علينا بما تقوم به معيشتنا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r8.claim: Different colors may mean red, white, and yellow; زرع covers all crops or different kinds such as wheat, barley, and sesame.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r8.anchor: مختلفا ألوانه: من أحمر وأبيض وأصفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r9.claim: يهيج means the crop approaches fruiting, or dries; مصفرا means its greenness and freshness have disappeared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r9.anchor: ثم يهيج: يقارب الثمار، فتراه مصفرا: أي زالت خضرته ونضارته.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r10.speaker: أبو بشر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r10.claim: Abu Bishr reads ثم يجعله with fatḥa on the lām; the author of al-Kamil calls the reading weak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو بشر: ثم يجعله، بالنصب في اللام. قال صاحب الكامل وهو ضعيف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r11.claim: The rain, crop growth, and its changing stages remind people of the Creator's wisdom and power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r11.anchor: إن في ذلك: أي فيما ذكر من إنزال المطر وإخراج الزرع به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r1.claim: The water is made to flow underground as springs and wells.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r1.anchor: ماء فسلكه} أدخل ذلك الماء، {ينابيع} عيونا وركايا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r2.speaker: الشعبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says every bit of water in the earth came down from the sky.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r2.anchor: قال الشعبي: كل ماء في الأرض فمن السماء نزل، {ثم يخرج به}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r3.claim: Water produces crops of different colors, including red, yellow, and green; they dry, turn yellow, and break into fragments, reminding people of understanding.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r3.anchor: {ثم يخرج به} أي: بالماء {زرعا مختلفا ألوانه} أحمر وأصفر وأخضر، {ثم يهيج} ييبس

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r1.claim: God sends the rain into the ground as springs and channels, or makes waters spring up there; yanābīʿ can mean a water source or the water that gushes from it, parsed as location or state.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r1.anchor: هي عيون ومجاري كائنة فيها، أو مياه نابعات فيها

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r2.claim: The crop's different colors may mean distinct species, such as wheat and barley, or varying hues such as green and red.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r3.claim: The crop dries completely, at which point it is ready to break away from its place of growth; it then yellows and crumbles.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r3.anchor: يتم جفافه لأنه إذا تم جفافه حان له أن يثور عن منبته

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r4.claim: The scene reminds observers either that a wise maker arranged it or that worldly life resembles this crop and should not deceive them; only people of understanding take the lesson.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r4.anchor: أو بأنه مثل الحياة الدنيا فلا تغتر بها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r1.speaker: الشعبي والضحاك
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r1.claim: Al-Shaʿbī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say that all earthly water descends from the sky to a rock, which distributes it into springs and wells.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r1.anchor: قال الشعبي والضحاك : كل ماء في الأرض من السماء ينزل إلى الصخرة ثم يقسم منها العيون والركايا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r2.claim: “Then” marks the delay between rainfall and the emergence of crops, while directing attention to the following demonstration.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r2.anchor: ولما كان إخراج النبات متراخيا عن نزول المطر , عبر بثم , وفيها أيضا تنبيه على تعظيم الأمر فيما تلاها بأنه محل الشاهد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r3.claim: The crops differ in kinds, qualities, temperaments, and tastes despite their common water, gathered from deep underground after soil forms.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r3.anchor: قال : { مختلفا ألوانه } أي في الأصناف والكيفيات والطبائع والطعوم وغير ذلك مع اتحاد الماء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r4.claim: The plant’s vigorous growth reaches its limit and then declines; exceeding a proper limit brings deficiency rather than benefit.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r4.anchor: قال إشارة إلى أن الخروج عن الحد غير محمود في شيء من الأشياء فإنه يعود عليه النقص

BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r5.claim: The vision is assigned to the Prophet, described as the best of creation, to intensify the invitation to contemplate the scene.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r5.anchor: وزاد في تعظيم هذا المعنى للحث على تدبره بإسناده إلى خير الخلق صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : { فتراه }

BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r6.claim: After its vigorous growth and completion, the plant turns yellow and begins drying, following its bloom, beauty, and freshness.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r6.anchor: وهو شدة ثورانه في نموه بعد التمام بتوقيع الانصرام أنك تراه { مصفرا } آخذا في الجفاف

BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r7.claim: God is explicitly the agent who makes the crop debris here, unlike the wording in al-Ḥadīd, because this passage emphasizes complete power while that one treats worldly life as nothingness.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r7.anchor: عبر بالجعل مسندا إليه سبحانه بخلاف آية الحديد التي عبر فيها بالكون لأن السياق ثم لأن الدنيا عدم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r8.claim: The crop’s death after growth proves that God can resurrect after annihilation, just as He originated beings from nothing.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r8.anchor: الدال بلا شك لكل من رآه على أن فاعله قادر على الإعادة لما يريد بعد الإبادة , كما قدر على الإيجاد من العدم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r9.claim: The plant’s course recalls resurrection and the afterlife: human life passes from water and infancy through old age to dust, which God gathers and raises like the plant.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r9.anchor: فإن النبات كالإنسان سواء , يكون ماء , ثم ينعقد بشرا , ثم يخرج طفلا , ثم يكون شابا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r10.claim: The reminder benefits people of exceptionally clear intellect; the author contrasts them with those outside the Prophet and his followers, whom he likens to animals.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r10.anchor: لأولي الألباب * } أي العقول الصافية جدا كما نبه بخصوص الخطاب

DURR-FULL:v7p218/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the water comes from veins in the earth rather than being sent down from the sky, and provocatively says anyone wanting to make salt water sweet should climb up.
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض} قال: ما أنزل الله

DURR-FULL:v7p218/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r2.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says the source of the water is from the sky.
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r2.anchor: عن الشعبي رضي الله عنه في قوله {فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض} أصله من السماء

DURR-FULL:v7p218/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses yanābīʿ as springs.
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج رضي الله عنه في قوله {فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض} قال: عيونا

DURR-FULL:v7p218/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r4.speaker: الكبي
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī says springs and wells are among the waters God sent down from the sky, adding that God knows best.
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r4.anchor: عن الكبي رضي الله عنه قال: العيون والركايا مما أنزل الله من السماء {فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r2.claim: The rain and growth passage begins the sūra’s Qur’an-and-Islam guidance theme, resumed in 39:22–23 after the excursus beginning at 39:2.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r2.anchor: استئناف ابتدائي انتقل به إلى غرض التنويه بالقرآن وما احتوى عليه من هدى الإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r3.claim: The rain sent down from heaven represents the Qur’an’s descent, which revives hearts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r3.anchor: فإنزال الماء من السماء تشبيه لإنزال القرآن لإحياء القلوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r4.claim: Water channeled into underground springs represents the Qur’an being conveyed to people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r4.anchor: وإسلاك الماء ينابيع في الأرض تشبيه لتبليغ القرآن للناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r5.claim: Crops of varied colors represent people differing as good or bad, beneficial or harmful.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r5.anchor: وإخراج الزرع المختلف الألوان تشبيه لحال اختلاف الناس من طيب وغيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r6.claim: The flourishing crop represents believers multiplying among the polytheists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r6.anchor: وهياج الزرع تشبيه لتكاثر المؤمنين بين المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r7.claim: The crop becoming dry debris also recalls death, in which beneficial and harmful people alike reach an end.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r7.anchor: فهو إدماج للتذكير بحالة الممات واستواء الناس فيها من نافع وضار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r8.claim: The juxtaposition of the rain parable with 39:22–23 signals the lesson drawn from it: the Qur’an-guided response parallels the growth of vegetation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r8.anchor: إشارة إلى العبرة من هذا التمثيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r9.claim: In a report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections, the Prophet likens his guidance and knowledge to abundant rain: receptive fertile soil yields growth, water-retaining soil benefits others, and barren land accepts neither; these represent people who learn and teach, transmit benefit, or reject guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r9.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r10.claim: Alternatively, the passage’s primary purpose is to prove God’s sole divinity from creation; the rain analogy to Qur’anic guidance is embedded within that proof.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى أصالة وإدماجا على عكس ما بينا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r11.claim: On either structural reading, the passage alludes to the possibility that God will bring people to life a second time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r11.anchor: وعلى كلا الوجهين أدمج في أثناء الكلام إيماء إلى إمكان إحياء الناس حياة ثانية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r1.claim: “People of understanding” are those who use their reason, benefit from the evidence, and believe; this implies that those who do not benefit from it are like people without minds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r1.anchor: وفي هذا تعريض بأن الذين لم يستفيدوا من الأدلة بمنزلة من عدموا العقول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r1.speaker: الشعبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r1.claim: Al-Sha'bi says everything found on earth comes down from heaven.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r1.anchor: قال الشعبي كل مافي الأرض فمن السماء ينزل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba says God made the water enter the earth and become springs that gush forth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي أدخله فجعله ينابيع أي عيونا تنبع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r3.claim: The plant's becoming hāʾij means that it dries.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r4.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r4.claim: Al-Asma'i says a plant is called hāʾij when its drying has fully run its course.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r4.anchor: قال الأصمعي يقال للثبت إذا تم جفافه قد هاج يهيج هيجا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
