IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda defines ḥuṭām as dried vegetation broken into pieces, like rufāt.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r5.anchor: فأما الحطام فقال أبو عبيدة هو ما يبس فتحات من النبات ومثله الرفات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r6.claim: Muqatil says the vegetation is a parable for worldly life and its adornments: what is green dries, changes, and perishes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل هذا مثل ضرب الدنيا بينا ترى النبت أخضر إذ تغير فيبس ثم هلك وكذلك الدنيا وزينتها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r7.speaker: غيره
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r7.claim: Another commentator takes the passage as an explanation demonstrating God's power.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p172#2/r7.anchor: وقال غيره هذا البيان للدلالة على قدرة الله عز وجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r1.claim: Water on earth originates in rain from the sky; God settles it in the ground, distributes it through the earth as He wills, and brings forth springs of varying size as needed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r1.anchor: فإذا أنزل الماء من السماء كمن في الأرض، ثم يصرفه تعالى في أجزاء الأرض كما يشاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says, in a report from Ikrima, that all earthly water came from the sky and underground veins alter it; he adds that one wishing to make salt sweet should raise it up.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة (2) ، عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى: {ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، وعامر الشعبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Amir al-Shaʿbi likewise say that all water in the earth originated in the sky.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r3.anchor: وكذا قال سعيد بن جبير، وعامر الشعبي: أن كل ماء في الأرض فأصله من السماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the water's source is snow that accumulates on mountains, settles in their depths, and feeds springs below.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p92#2/r4.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: أصله من الثلج يعني: أن الثلج يتراكم على الجبال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93/r1.claim: The crop's differing colors include its varying forms, tastes, scents, and benefits.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93/r2.claim: After freshness and youth the plant ages, turns yellow as dryness overtakes it, and finally becomes brittle and dry.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93/r2.anchor: أي: بعد نضارته وشبابه يكتهل (1) {فتراه مصفرا} ، قد خالطه اليبس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93/r3.claim: The changing crop teaches that worldly life turns from beauty to ugliness, youth to frail old age, and then death; the fortunate person fares better after death. Ibn Kathir compares it to the world's example in the Cave.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93/r3.anchor: تكون خضرة نضرة حسناء، ثم تعود عجوزا شوهاء، والشاب يعود شيخا هرما كبيرا ضعيفا

JISHUMI:v8p6052/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r7.claim: Sulūk is entering by passing through something; one says salaktuhu fīhi, as when threading a needle, rather than salaka fī al-Islām.
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r7.anchor: السلوك: دخول بمرور على الشيء؛ ولذلك يقال: دنجل في الإسلام، ولا يقال: سلك في الإسلام

JISHUMI:v8p6052/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r8.claim: Yanābīʿ is the plural of yanbūʿ, springs at the place where water emerges.
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r8.anchor: والينابيع: جمع ينبوع، وهي العيون في المكان الذي ينبع منه الماء

JISHUMI:v8p6052/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r9.claim: Hayj describes intense agitation and turning; it also means drying, motion, turmoil, rising blood, sexual arousal, or longing.
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r9.anchor: والهيج: شدة الاضطراب بالانقلاب، هاج هيجا وهيجانا، والهيج: الجفاف

JISHUMI:v8p6052/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r10.claim: Ḥaṭm is breaking a dry thing, and maḥṭūm is something broken.
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r10.anchor: والحطم: كسر الشيء اليابس، والمحطوم: المكسور

JISHUMI:v8p6052/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r11.claim: Hell is called al-Ḥuṭama because it breaks everything; al-Ḥaṭīm in Mecca is named for the broken-off portion beside the Kaʿba’s water spout, according to al-Naḍr.
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r11.anchor: الحطيم بمكة، قال النضر: لأن البيت رفع وترك ذاك محطوما

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r9.claim: Alam tara is jussive: lam removes the original final yāʾ from tarā, while the rāʾ retains its fatḥa.
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r9.anchor: (ألم تر) جزم، علامته ذهاب الياء؛ لأن أصله ألم ترى، فسقطت الياء للجزم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r1.claim: The water sent down is rain.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r1.anchor: هو المطر . وقيل : كل ماء في الأرض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r2.claim: An alternative view says all water on earth comes from the sky, descending to a rock before God apportions it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r2.anchor: وقيل : كل ماء في الأرض فهو من السماء ينزل منها إلى الصخرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r3.claim: The verb means that God inserts and orders the water into springs and into channels and courses through the earth, like veins in bodies.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r3.anchor: فأدخله ونظمه { ينابيع فى الارض } عيونا ومسالك ومجاري كالعروق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r4.claim: The differing colors include the plants’ forms and hues, such as green, red, yellow, and white, as well as crop varieties such as wheat, barley, and sesame.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r4.anchor: هيئاته من خضرة وحمرة وصفرة وبياض وغير ذلك ، وأصنافه من بر وشعير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r5.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī glosses يهيج as completing its drying: then the crop is ready to rise from its roots and disappear.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r5.anchor: عن الأصمعي ؛ لأنه إذا تم جفافه حان له أن يثور عن منابته ويذهب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r6.claim: حطاما means fragments and dry plant debris.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r6.anchor: فتاتا ودرينا { إن فى ذلك لذكرى } لتذكيرا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r7.claim: The changing crop reminds people that a wise maker exists and that creation follows determination and management, rather than idleness or neglect.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r7.anchor: لتذكيرا وتنبيها ، على أنه لا بد من صانع حكيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r8.claim: The crop’s cycle may also stand as a likeness for worldly life, as in the examples at 10:24 and 18:45.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مثلا للدنيا ، كقوله تعالى : { إنما مثل الحيواة الدنيا }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p123#4/r9.claim: The phrase is also read مصفارا.

MUQATIL:39:21-23/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r1.claim: God makes the rain into springs and wells, then brings forth plants of varied colors that dry, yellow, and break apart.

MUQATIL:39:21-23/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r2.claim: Ḥuṭām means destroyed or perished, as in the wording of 27:18; the world's flourishing is similarly followed by decay and ruin.

MUQATIL:39:21-23/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r3.claim: The plant's rise and decay are a worldly parable and a reminder to reflect for people of understanding.
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r3.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله فى الدنيا كمثل النبت، بينما هو أخضر إذ تغير فيبس، ثم هلك، فكذلك تهلك الدنيا بعد بهجتها وزينتها
